recipes.name: Super Easy Chicken Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) can chopped green chile peppers
1 roasted chicken, bones and skin removed, meat torn into bite-size pieces
1 (8 ounce) package shredded Monterey Jack cheese

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in onions, and cook until softened and translucent, about 3 minutes. Pour in chicken broth, great Northern beans, chopped chiles, and torn chicken. Season with cumin, chili powder, and cayenne pepper. Increase heat to medium-high to bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in sour cream and simmer for 5 minutes. To serve, ladle into bowls and sprinkle with Monterey Jack cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Super Easy Chicken Chili
raw_recipe.description: This quick, spicy chicken chili uses one of those hot, cooked rotisserie chickens from the supermarket along with a couple of cans. It’s all ready to eat 35 minutes after you get home!

review.reviewBody: HOLY GUACAMOLE!!! I read the reviews before making this and believed that the addition of the sour cream would tone down the mega heat from all the spices. DO NOT BE FOOLED BY THIS ADVICE! We really enjoy hot and spicy foods but this was WAY TOO HOT! I did eat it and I did finish it, but it was a bit painful to do. The spices got to my sinuses and my nose was running so much that I went through 7 tissues during dinner. And the ceiling fan that was keeping us nice & cool seemed as if it was no longer functioning. We had sweat dripping from us by the time we were through. The only reason I'm giving this 4 stars is because it does have potential. I will try it again, but I'll cut back on the cayenne by at least half.

I always read reviews, so I knew to cut down on the spices. The chili is more of a white chili when the cayenne is cut down. It is a pretty easy recipe.
Since it's only us 2, HALVED the recipe. Did not have green chilis, so I used half of a good-sized poblano and fried it with the onion. Cut up 1 and 1/2 chicken breasts (left over from last night's dinner). Used 1 T cumin, 1 T chili powder and 1/2 tsp cayenne. Broiled a slice of Colby Jack on top of each of the 3 bowls it made. I'm a wimp about heat, and it was spicy but good to me. My man from Texas thought it was perfect. Will save this one! Ty

We loved this. I used a rotisserie chicken. I cut the cayenne back to 1 teaspoon. I can’t even imagine what 2 tablespoons would be like. I also added a can of drained corn. I used two cans of chicken broth because I didn’t want to throw out half a can. It was perfectly fine. If you want a thick chili, don’t use two cans.

I wanted a super easy chicken chili base recipe that I could build upon depending on what was in the pantry. This is THE perfect recipe once I adjusted a few things! I decreased the cumin to 1 tablespoon, chili powder to 2 tablespoons, and cayenne to 1 teaspoon to keep the spicy kick. I also add 4 ounces of cream cheese to round out the flavors. Delish!

Everyone in my family loved this! Even my three picky children who "don't like beans!" I cut the cyanne pepper to 1/4 tsp, used black beans and used fat free sour cream. I also cut up boneless skinless chicken breast and cooked it with the broth, chili's and spices in the crockpot, one hour before serving I added black beans, and 15 min before serving I added the sour cream. WE LOVED THIS!

I believe the tablespoons was a typo. It should definitely be teaspoons as I was thinking when putting in tablespoons of the stout spices. I will dilute my pot with tomatoes (Rotel), water, and more beans)

READ THIS!! 
First things first, I love this chili! 
Making this exactly as the recipe says, is a wildly spicy idea. I think the original recipe has tablespoons mistaken for teaspoons. When I first made it it was so hot we could hardly eat it (but had good flavor). So I cut the spice in half; still pretty freaking hot. So I cut it back a little bit more the next time I made it; much better. If you use teaspoons instead of tablespoons it will still be spicy, but in a normal range of spicy. 
YUMMMMMMM

This was a great base to work from for using a leftover roasted chicken. Used cannellini beans instead of northern, diced tomato w. jalapeno instead of green chilies, no cumin, 1 tsp oregano & 1 tsp minced garlic (based on reviews & similar recipes). I cut the recipe in half & still cut back to 1-1/2 tsp cayenne and 1-1/2 tsp chili powder, left out sour cream, so the end result was the perfect amount of heat for someone who likes medium spicy. I'm not familiar with the level of heat from green chilies but I can see how just the original spice content would have made this extremely hot so....Beware! This was a nice healthy quick meal so I will definitely keep for future, thanks!

I made 3 good size servings. I read the reviews that said it was super hot so I toned it down too. We thought it was awesome and will for sure make it again. I used all the rotisserie pieces leftover after just 2 of us ate the chicken the night before. I used 1 can of beans 1 small can of green chili's (4.5 oz) because that's all I had, 2 TBS ground cumin, 2 tsp chili powder, 2 tsp. cayenne pepper, I added one 6 oz can of tomato paste. We used sour cream and cheese as a garnish on top. But I used cottage cheese instead of sour cream. It served 2 very healthy servings and then one very healthy serving the next day for my boyfriend who said it was even better. Next time I will make it for my boys who are very picky.

This recipe is really good, but one look at the spice list and I knew I had to change it up a little. 2 tablespoons of cayenne is waaaaaay too spicy for the normal palate, and I've found it gets hotter if you've got leftovers! So I used 2 tablespoons of cumin and 1/2 tsp of the cayenne. The heat level was just right. Might want to try it with some corn next time... :D

Easy and delicious! I put everything into the crockpot in the AM and it was ready to eat by supper. I used one teaspoon of cayenne and it was perfect -- just spicy enough. It's not as heavy as beef chili, but still has a nice chili taste. I'll be making this often.
Wish I had read reviews first. I only added one of the tablespoons of Cheyenne and still way too hot. I solved by doubling the recipe. It's great now, but that's a lot of chili for two old people!

4 Alarm FIRE!!! Way too spicy. Practically unbearable to eat. I gave up a third of the way through a small bowl of it. Added more sour cream and sugar trying to soften the blow. Topped with cheese and tortilla strips. NOTHING HELPED!!! A waste of high priced chicken and beans!! I’m so disappointed because it’s such a simple recipe and with less spruce intensity it’s probably good. But, I’m curious…did Megs even taste test this before sharing??!
This recipe was tasty but should have gone with my gut and added less cayenne, I love spicy but it was definitely too spicy for me and my kids.

Needed a quick recipe for a cold rainy day and stumbled on this one. I happened to have all the ingredients with the exception of the chicken, I just cooked up chicken tenders and added it to the broth mixture. I also kept the cayenne pepper to a minimum. Fabulous flavor and is now our #1 chicken chili recipe!
I love it!!! Instead of all the spices I just used 2 TLBS of chili powder and it was perfect.
This was fast and very yummy with tortillas!! I read the reviews about the spices and I only adjusted them to our liking and this is a keeper!

Good and easy! I took the advice of others and cut down the spices. I only used 1/2 tsp cumin and 2T chili powder and cayenne. I served it with crackers and cheese. It was spicy and flavorful. I'll be making it again.
This has become a family favorite. I used a chili seasoning packet instead of the spices. Everyone loved it!! I used the "hot" seasoning packet. It was perfect.

Way too much spice. I added Mac and cheese and made it more like chil-Mac. The only reason I gave 3 stars was bc my 2 year old liked it. But she tends to like spice. I omitted the cayenne pepper all together and added more broth.
